title: Cernos
extract:
The Cernos is a  Tenno Bow, and the first one available to new players that deals mainly  Impact damage over another type.
This weapon can be sold for  10,500. It is also a weapon crafting ingredient for  Mutalist Cernos.

Acquisition
The Cernos's blueprint can be purchased from the Market.

Tips
Despite what its description says, the Cernos is most effective against  Grineer , which are primarily armored, not shielded. Its damage spread being weighted primarily towards Impact means the majority of the weapon's damage will inherit the element's Faction Damage Bonus against them, dealing solid damage even through their armor.
Impact's status effect of reducing the target's Mercy threshold also logically counteracts their armor, allowing heavy enemies to be executed even with most of their health remaining, once their Overguard is broken, after suffering enough Impact procs.
While the Cernos has a low base status chance relative to its rate of fire and projectile count, this can easily be fixed with modding.  Rifle Aptitude will bring it up to a respectable 34%, which can be rolled multiple times per shot by adding multishot mods, such as  Split Chamber.
Adding Corrosive damage to the Cernos is a good idea, enhancing how much damage it can do to Grineer enemies even further.
The Cernos is also strong against enemies of the  Scaldra and  Anarchs factions, though by the time the player is able to fight these enemies, they will likely have replaced the Cernos with a superior weapon, such as one of its upgraded counterparts.
The Cernos is very statistically similar to the  Paris and  Dread, two other Bows that become available by the time it is. The three primarily vary in which physical element they are most weighted towards, though the Dread will generally be the last of the three a new player obtains unless they're especially lucky. Thus, if the player has used either of the other two Bows, they will likely know how to use the Cernos.
With a maxed  Critical Delay mod, the Cernos' critical chance will increase to 103.3%. This breaks the 100% critical chance threshold, guaranteeing every hit will be a critical hit and giving the weapon a very small chance to "orange crit", whereupon a critical hit will have its critical multiplier doubled.
Using a maxed Critical Delay however will also drastically reduce the Cernos's fire rate, due to mods that modify this stat having their effect doubled on Bows, making each Cernos arrow take a long time to draw back. This can be countered with the usage of a fire rate mod, such as  Speed Trigger.
Even with only  Point Strike, the Cernos will reach 90% critical chance, causing its hits to be critical far more often than they aren't.
If this modding avenue is chosen, adding as many critical damage mods to the Cernos as possible is advised, as they will apply on every hit for a very large damage increase.
At the Mastery Rank the Cernos is unlocked, the Dread and  Cinta are also capable of exceeding 100% critical chance. Of the three, the Cernos is generally the easiest to obtain.

Trivia
The name "Cernos" means "horn" in Gaulish.
Despite being more effective against the highly-armored  Grineer, the Cernos's description says it's effective against "highly shielded enemies", implying it's effective against the Corpus instead, who are instead vulnerable to  Puncture damage. This is an artifact from before Update 36.0, where Damage 2.0's health types system instead made Impact damage stronger against energy shielding regardless of faction, while Puncture was stronger against most forms of armor. After the update, which replaced this system with Damage 3.0's faction multipliers and swapped the Corpus and Grineer's vulnerabilities, the Cernos's description was not updated to compensate, and still has not been as of Hotfix 41.1.2 (2-17-2026).
Being an Impact oriented bow, the Cernos uses arrows with a mace-like head, with a larger impact area. This spreads the kinetic energy of the arrows across a wider area, creating a blunt impact, hence its damage distribution.
Despite this, the Cernos's arrows can still pin enemies they kill to walls. Judging by the hole in the middle of the head, it's possible the arrows are hollow to house a spring-loaded punch system that fires a spike upon impact, though no such animation exists in-game if Captura mode's camera is used to watch the arrows mid-flight.
The Prisma Arrows skin highly resembles the Cernos's arrows, and can be equipped to any Bow-type weapon.
As of Update 30.3 (2021-05-25), the Cernos has the most variations of all weapons, having a total of 5 weapons in its family; the normal  Cernos,  Rakta Cernos,  Cernos Prime,  Mutalist Cernos, and  Proboscis Cernos.
The Cernos is the first weapon to have two upgraded forms, with both its Mutalist and Proboscics variants requiring the other form respectively in order to be built.
The Cernos is also one of the few weapons to have variants that are considered separate weapons for the sake of mechanics like Riven mods, rather than direct variants, that aren't simply an akimbo version of the weapon. The  Quanta is another.
